title: UCO Bank - 532505 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: UCO Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 26.77% YoY to Rs 786 crore; advances grew 24.70%, well above the 12-14% guidance.
summary.overview: UCO Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 786 crore, up 26.77% YoY from Rs 620 crore, with operating profit of Rs 1,872 crore (up 16.04%). Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Gross NPA fell 60 bps YoY to 1.96% and net NPA to 0.18%, both within guidance. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -60 bps YoY; NNPA -25 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 30.23% YoY; housing loan growth above 20% YoY with average home-loan ticket up from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 29.59% YoY; agri slippages rose to Rs 205 crore in Q2 from Rs 73 crore in Q1, but were below Rs 238 crore a year ago.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 20.32% YoY; management sees scope for more growth here.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; sanctioned but undisbursed corporate pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore.

segments.name: RAM portfolio
segments.commentary: RAM portfolio is Rs 1,68,736 crore, up 26.92% YoY, and its share of advances has crossed 65% against the 62-65% guidance.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Hong Kong and Singapore branches are operating; GIFT City IBU opened in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guidance of 12-14% for FY27 was kept; management said it aims to grow above guidance but will not revise it mid-year.
Deposit growth guidance of 10-12% was exceeded (actual 14%+).
GNPA guidance is below 2% by 31 March 2027; already at 1.96%.
Net NPA guidance is below 0.25% for the year; already at 0.18%.
Global NIM guidance of 2.80-2.90% was exceeded (3.00%); management expects to sustain NIM above guidance with repo pass-through.
Credit cost guidance is below 0.75% for FY27; Q2 is 0.65%.
Cost-to-income expected to be around 50% for the full year and possibly below 50% next year.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027 estimated at about Rs 3,200 crore+ requirement; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 3,439 after adding 27 branches in the quarter; business per branch Rs 185 crore vs Rs 161 crore a year ago.
Business per employee Rs 30 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.
GIFT City IBU opened in Q2; three international branches (Hong Kong, Singapore, GIFT City).
Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.
Seven processes automated via RPA; digital marketing solution onboarded; customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches.
Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.
demand_pricing: Advances growth came from all segments; RAM share has crossed 65%, and management expects it to hold around 65% with corporate growth also continuing.
Corporate sanctioned pipeline of about Rs 10,000 crore is undisbursed; disbursement depends on corporates' acceptance of lending rates and capex plans.
About 66% of advances are linked to external benchmark (repo/EBLR); a 25 bps repo hike was passed on immediately to these loans.
Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.
Gold loan yield is about 9% (slightly below) and unchanged QoQ.
Housing loan growth above 20% YoY from both volume and ticket size; second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are small.
Domestic yield on advances 8.11%; global yield 7.79%; cost of funds 4.44%, up slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries from written-off accounts fell to Rs 301 crore from Rs 1,018 crore; is this a normalised rate, and what is the treasury outlook given rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the June quarter included a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery from one large account; excluding it, June recovery was about Rs 233 crore, so Rs 301 crore is the normalised run-rate. On treasury, management said yield hardening pressures profitability, but ~66% of advances are repo/EBLR-linked, so NII gains should offset treasury losses; FVTPL book is small.

qa_highlights.question: Slippages rose from Rs 428 crore to Rs 538 crore and SMA-1 rose from Rs 228 crore to Rs 437 crore; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were Rs 549 crore in the quarter per management; the rise is mainly half-yearly crop-loan agriculture marking in September. SMA-1 and SMA-2 (Rs 1 crore and above) stood at 0.42% vs 0.77% a year ago, with a QoQ uptick described as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates be raised, and with what lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate need to raise deposit rates; current term deposit rates maintained. Any hike would apply only to new deposits and renewals, decided later based on deposit requirement.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in corporate stance, and will the bank raise its credit growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; RAM share crossed 65% (guidance 62-65%) and is expected to hold around 65%. Corporate sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore, dependent on lending rates and capex. Guidance of 12-14% kept; management aims to exceed it but will not revise mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition estimate for 1 April 2027 and has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition requirement estimated at about Rs 2,500 crore in one answer and Rs 3,200 crore-plus in another; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions, including COVID provisions of Rs 530 crore, extra provisions of Rs 341 crore and about Rs 1,600 crore ECL-specific. Estimate not materially changed from three months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan yield and how is it trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan yield is around 9%, slightly below; no change QoQ as no rate changes were made. Any EBLR-linked gold loans will reprice with the repo hike.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating expenses rise by about Rs 160 crore, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is normal, reflecting IT investment, physical infrastructure and network expansion, plus a lag in opex growth in earlier quarters; expected to stay in a similar range, depending on transaction volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income outlook for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 0.65% vs guidance below 0.75%, with ECL provisioning of Rs 570 crore in the quarter and accelerated NPA provisioning to bring NNPA to 0.18%. Cost-to-income was 50.39% (about 45% excluding the June one-off effect); expected around 50% for FY27 and possibly below 50% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Second-hand car loan growth and yield, and housing ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are a small share of car loans; management will work out numbers. Average home-loan ticket rose from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh, with growth from both volume and ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Is NII growth enough to offset treasury stress, and what NIM is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said repo-linked NII growth (about 66% of advances) would more than offset treasury stress, and that FVTPL exposure is small. Global NIM was 3.00% and domestic 3.19%, against guidance of 2.80-2.90%; management expects to sustain NIM above guidance.

risks_watch: Treasury losses from hardening yields; FVTPL book is small but MTM impact depends on the yield path and any further RBI repo action.
Asset quality: quarterly slippage of Rs 549 crore (0.85%), with agri slippage Rs 205 crore and SMA-1/2 up QoQ to Rs 437 crore; watch whether the September agri marking reverses or persists in March.
Recovery from written-off accounts normalising at about Rs 300 crore per quarter, down from the Rs 1,018 crore a year ago, as large accounts are largely resolved.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027: requirement of about Rs 2,500-3,200 crore plus, with Rs 2,500 crore already provided; any further top-up depends on profitability.
Deposit mobilisation: CASA ratio slipped to 36.77% and deposit rates are unchanged, while advances growth of 24.70% far exceeds 10-12% deposit guidance.
Corporate growth conversion: Rs 10,000 crore sanctioned corporate pipeline remains undisbursed and depends on lending rates and capex; watch the RAM-share cap near 65%.
key_quotes: So, this is the normal recovery, and this quarter we don’t have any such big recovery account, which was a one-off in the last quarter.
So, overall, the asset quality has been maintained.
We are ready to take up the growth, whatever the credit growth we can take up in all the sectors.
But, yes, as we move ahead in the year, we will see and we will try to grow more than that, of course.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profitability and asset quality, with management repeatedly saying results are ahead of guidance. Cautious and somewhat defensive on slippages, SMA-1 rise, treasury yield pressure and whether guidance will be revised, saying it will not change guidance mid-year.

adds.what: 27 new branches added in Q2 FY27, taking network to 3,439
GIFT City IBU (international banking unit) opened in Q2 FY27

growth.why: Advances guidance of 12-14% was held though Q2 advances grew 24.70%; management aims to beat it, backed by a ~Rs 10,000 crore undisbursed corporate pipeline, 27 new branches and the GIFT City IBU, with no capacity figures for utilisation or new capacity.
